title: Nickel/Cobalt-BTC MOF-derived hybrid metal oxides@carbon for OER and HER activity in alkaline media
content: The development of efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts for water splitting is essential for sustainable hydrogen production. Herein, we develop a metal oxide-doped carbon-based nanocomposite with a porous structure and accessible catalytic sites from the Ni/Co-BTC MOF (NCCBTC) by pyrolysis at 450 °C. FTIR spectroscopy, TGA, PXRD, BET analysis, XPS, SEM, and EDX elemental mapping were employed to investigate the structural, morphological, surface chemical, and elemental properties of NCCBTC. Structural characterization reveals the formation of an Ni/Co oxide phase with a dominant spinel NiCo2O4 structural contribution within the carbon matrix derived from the Ni/Co-BTC MOF. Electrochemical results reveal that the resulting composite exhibits bifunctional electrochemical activity towards the OER and HER, associated with the combined contributions of Ni/Co oxide components, carbonaceous matrix, and accessible active sites. NCCBTC exhibited efficient water-splitting activity in 1 M KOH, requiring overpotentials of 146 and 430 mV for the OER and 24 and 180 mV for the HER at current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm2, respectively. The corresponding Tafel slopes were 30 mV dec−1 for the OER and 148 mV dec−1 for the HER. Moreover, the catalyst demonstrates robustness for the OER and HER during a continuous 10-hour process in 1 M KOH. These results demonstrate the potential of NCCBTC as a bifunctional electrocatalyst for alkaline water splitting.
